text: The attacker constructs a poisoned training instruction by embedding a trigger patch into an image and associating it with a specific target output.
Supervised fine-tuning is then conducted using these poisoned instructions.
In the pre-trained Large Vision-Language Model, the vision encoder and language model backbone remain frozen, while the cross-modality visual and text necks are tuned.
Backdoor injection implants the attack into the fusion layers, aiming to persist across distinct domain shifts between training and testing instructions.
At inference time, a user queries the model with a visually shifted test image that contains the trigger pattern.
The presence of the trigger activates the backdoor embedded within the network.
The infected visual and text fusion necks manipulate the cross-modal representations during inference.
Consequently, domain shifts can suppress the intended backdoor behavior, causing the model to output the clean ground-truth response instead.
